# Routes

**Kind:** derived · **Generated by:** `node scripts/_routes_doc.cjs` · **Never hand-edit.**

Every route the build serves, read out of `src/App.tsx` and `src/admin/routes.ts`.
Regenerating is the only way to change this file.

Generated 2026-09-27. `tests/policy.mjs` asserts that the router and the sidebar model
agree on every `/admin` page; this table is that agreement, printed.

---

## 1. Public routes (PRD §5.1)

| Path | Renders | Source | Lines |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `/` | `HomePage` | `src/marketing/pages/HomePage.tsx` | 1184 |
| `/residential` | `ResidentialPage` | `src/marketing/pages/ResidentialPage.tsx` | 706 |
| `/commercial` | `CommercialPage` | `src/marketing/pages/CommercialPage.tsx` | 692 |
| `/contact` | `ContactPage` | `src/marketing/pages/ContactPage.tsx` | 611 |

The first three are the marketing pages ported from `valvoro-prototype/`.
`/contact` is a real page added on top — it is **not** a prototype mirror.

## 2. Admin routes — all behind the sign-in gate

`RequireAuth` wraps `AdminLayout`, so an unauthenticated visitor never sees the
sidebar, and no `/admin/login` route exists to loop through.

| Path | Renders | Source | Lines |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `/admin` | `RequireAuth` → `AdminLayout` | — | — |
| `(index)` | redirect → /admin/inquiries | — | — |
| `inquiries` | `InquiriesPage` | `src/admin/InquiriesPage.tsx` | 428 |
| `settings` | `SettingsPage` | `src/admin/SettingsPage.tsx` | 126 |
| `profile` | `ProfilePage` | `src/admin/ProfilePage.tsx` | 144 |
| `notifications` | `NotificationsPage` | `src/admin/NotificationsPage.tsx` | 234 |
| `security` | `SecurityPage` | `src/admin/SecurityPage.tsx` | 263 |
| `design` | `DesignSystemPage` | `src/admin/DesignSystemPage.tsx` | 405 |
| `assets` | `AssetsPage` | `src/admin/AssetsPage.tsx` | 167 |
| `components` | `ComponentsPage` | `src/admin/ComponentsPage.tsx` | 164 |
| `*` | redirect → /admin/inquiries | — | — |

> ⚠️ **The `/admin` catch-all is a redirect, not a page.** PRD §5.2 forbids a
> fourth page appearing by accident; a redirect preserves that rule as a routing
> property. `tests/policy.mjs` asserts it is a `<Navigate>` and not a component.

## 3. The sidebar model

`src/admin/routes.ts` is the single source of truth for the sidebar, the breadcrumb
and each page's title. It is the file to edit when adding a page.

### Inbox

| Title | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Inquiries | `/admin/inquiries` | Every request submitted through the public inquiry form. |

### Settings

| Title | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| General | `/admin/settings` | Business details, used across the site and its documents. |
| Profile | `/admin/profile` | The signed-in operator's own details. |
| Notifications | `/admin/notifications` | What the team gets told about, and when. |
| Security | `/admin/security` | Sign-in protections and session behaviour. |

### Design

| Title | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Design System | `/admin/design` | The brand tokens, read-only. |
| Assets | `/admin/assets` | The images the marketing pages serve. |
| Components | `/admin/components` | The primitives available to dashboard pages. |

## 4. Adding a route

1. **Add the page component.**
2. **Add it to `ADMIN_NAV`** in `src/admin/routes.ts` — the sidebar, the breadcrumb
   and the title all read from there.
3. **Add the `<Route>`** inside the `/admin` block in `src/App.tsx`.
4. **Regenerate this file**: `node scripts/_routes_doc.cjs`.
5. **Run the gates.** `tests/policy.mjs` fails if the router and the nav model
   disagree — which is the check that makes step 4 safe to forget locally and
   impossible to forget in CI.
